notes: Patterns are Python re, matched case-insensitively per line unless 'cs' is true. 'leg' entries feed the lethal-trifecta verdict. Standalone rules carry their own severity. 'negation_safe' rules are suppressed when the words just before the match negate them, so a skill that says "never use sudo" is not reported for using sudo.

legs.title: reads browser cookie or password stores
drives a browser or scrapes pages
reads issue, PR, or mail bodies written by other people

legs.pattern: git push|gh gist create|gh release upload|gh api\s[^\n]*-X\s*(POST|PUT|PATCH)|gh (issue|pr) (create|comment)
legs.title: writes to a remote repository or gist

legs.pattern: aws s3 cp|s3\.upload|gsutil cp|az storage blob upload|\bscp\s|\brsync\s[^\n]*::?
legs.title: uploads to remote storage

rules.title: downloads a remote script and executes it
rules.why: The code that actually runs is whatever that URL serves at the moment you run it. Nothing you review here binds it.

rules.title: pipes a remote download into an interpreter
rules.why: The inline program decides what happens to the download. Whether that is parsing it or running it cannot be read off the command line, so read the program. This is the same line RCE-PIPE-SHELL would call critical if it could prove the download gets executed.

rules.title: evaluates remotely fetched text as code
rules.why: Same as piping to a shell, with an extra layer to make review harder.

rules.title: decodes an encoded blob and runs it
rules.why: Encoding exists here only to stop a human from reading it.

rules.title: contains a long opaque encoded blob
rules.why: Nobody can review 220+ characters of base64 by eye. Ask what it is before you install.

rules.title: encodes local files or environment before sending them
rules.why: Encoding on the way out is not compression, it is packaging for transport.

rules.title: tells the agent to ignore its previous instructions
rules.why: A skill is instructions. A skill that overrides your instructions is an injection you installed on purpose.

rules.pattern: (do not|don't|never) (tell|inform|mention|show|reveal|notify|surface|disclose)[^\n]{0,40}(user|human|operator)|without (telling|informing|asking) the (user|human)|do not mention this (skill|file|step)|silently (send|upload|post|delete|run)|keep this (secret|hidden|between us)
rules.title: tells the agent to hide something from you
rules.why: There is no legitimate reason for a skill to withhold its own behaviour from the person running it.

rules.title: tells the agent to skip asking you
rules.why: Removing the confirmation step removes the only place a bad action gets caught.

rules.title: disables the agent's permission system
rules.why: This turns off the containment that is supposed to survive a prompt injection.

rules.title: requests unrestricted shell access
rules.why: Every other control in this list is downstream of this one.

rules.title: writes to your agent's config or installs a hook
rules.why: This outlives the session. Deleting the skill does not remove it.

rules.title: installs itself into your shell or a scheduler
rules.why: Persistence outside the agent entirely.

rules.pattern: \b(pip[0-9.]*|uv pip) install\b|npm i(nstall)? -g|\bnpx -y\b|\bbunx\b|cargo install|go install|brew install
rules.title: installs software when it runs
rules.why: The dependency tree you get is resolved at run time, not at review time.

rules.title: runs destructive commands
rules.why: Blast radius if anything upstream goes wrong.

rules.title: asks for root
rules.why: Anything that goes wrong past this line goes wrong as root.

rules.title: throws away uncommitted work
rules.why: Recoverable only if you had committed. Often shows up in "recovery" instructions.

rules.title: pulls from a moving reference instead of a pinned commit
rules.why: What you reviewed and what runs tomorrow are different files.

rules.title: declares no allowed-tools
rules.why: The field is optional in the Agent Skills spec, so most skills omit it. It means the runtime, not the skill, decides what it can reach.

rules.title: a file could not be read at all
rules.why: Permission denied, or it changed under the scan. No rule has looked inside it, and if it could not be hashed it is not in the lock either, so --check may not notice it changing again. This is the one place a payload can sit where nothing here has looked, so look yourself.

rules.title: a file was too large to read
rules.why: It is hashed and covered by --check, but no rule has looked inside it. Read it yourself or ask why a skill ships a file that big.

rules.title: a symlink points outside the skill
rules.why: Whatever reads this skill reads that file instead. It is not followed here, and it should not be followed by your agent either.

rules.title: the directory you named is a symlink
rules.why: Followed, because you named it and pointing a skills directory at a dotfiles checkout is ordinary. Links found inside a skill are not followed, because the skill chose those. What actually got scanned is the target, so check that it is what you meant to audit.

rules.title: the skill contains a symlink
rules.why: It stays inside the skill, but a link is an indirection that review tends to skip. It is hashed by its target path, so retargeting it shows up as drift.

rules.title: a line is too long to review or to match in full
rules.why: Real code and real prose do not run to thousands of characters on one line. The line is matched in overlapping windows and again with its padding compressed, but full pattern coverage cannot be guaranteed at this length, so the verdict does not get to be quiet about it. The line was written to be unreadable.
